tool_input.prompt:
Draw ONE full-body Guarin, a weary returning household knight from the Royans/Isere lands in 1101, as a dark, cute-proportioned isometric game character. Create an entirely NEW drawing from this text, with no input image. His oversized helmet/head takes about 43 percent of his total standing height: a tiny stocky torso, very short arms and stubby legs beneath a huge head, approximately 2.3 head heights tall overall. Preserve this exact costume and loadout: fully enclosed dull-iron cylindrical greathelm with flat circular crown, two plain vertical riveted reinforcing strips down the faceplate sides, with a bare flat crown free of crossed strips, one narrow black visor slit and a few small round breathing holes; fine RING mail shirt and sleeves beneath a ragged faded wine-red scarf and short cape, ragged wine-red waist cloth, one brown leather belt with plain rectangular buckle, taupe/brown cloth wraps at forearms and lower legs, plain brown gloves and short rounded brown leather boots. His face and eyes are entirely concealed. His right hand on the viewer's left holds a short, perfectly straight double-edged arming sword down diagonally: disk pommel, simple brown grip, straight crossguard, straight symmetrical blade, and centered point all rigidly aligned. His left hand on the viewer's right carries the SAME medium-sized elongated kite shield of weathered taupe wood, plain dull iron rim and one narrow faded wine-red vertical panel. The greathelm and simplified wraps are deliberate established character-design exceptions; this is a regional story character, not a claim that every part is an excavated French costume of 1101. Keep ring mail rather than scales or plate, with restrained local materials, no imported royal ornament, invented heraldic order, symbols, crests or new costume pieces.
Use the SAME elevated orthographic gameplay view in this comparison, camera about 40 degrees ABOVE THE HORIZONTAL GROUND, looking down on a character facing diagonally toward the lower-right, with the visor bending toward the image right and the sword crossing down from the viewer-left hand to its tip at the lower-right. His vertical barrel helmet has a level horizontal circular top, seen as a DEEP ellipse with minor axis about 64 percent of its major axis; expose the top, shoulders, shield rim and boot tops coherently, rather than an eye-level portrait. His head stays upright. Keep both feet, sword tip and shield tip visible in a neutral idle stance, centered with generous margin against a simple flat charcoal background and small grounding shadow. Use soot gray iron, muted taupe/brown, dark dried-wine cloth and sparse bone-gray highlights, solemn but endearing. This must preserve oversized-head/small-body charm rather than adult human anatomy. Rendering is the ONLY variable: costume, color placement, equipment, pose, view and proportions remain as above. One character, one view, no scene, captions, text, logo, panels, large eyes or bright glowing details.

Keep that same lower-right facing pose: the shield is at image RIGHT and the sword blade crosses IN FRONT OF HIS SHORT LEGS toward the lower-right; the crown has no crossed bands. RENDERING C: a rough 2D charcoal-and-etching drawing tinted with muted wine and taupe washes. Build volume with large rough charcoal hatch masses, broken ragged scratch lines, bold stippled shadow shapes and scraped dusty highlights, with abundant large quiet shapes between marks and forceful visible charcoal texture that differs clearly from polished ink linework. Angular abbreviated facets, rasped silhouettes and expressive hand-drawn marks give it a much more raw, print-like construction than smooth cel ink or soft gouache. Keep the identical cute huge-head/tiny-body proportions and fixed costume, not realistic anatomy or a medieval manuscript copy. Subtle pixel-adjacent clustering only, not a coarse mosaic. The result should feel like a dark, colored charcoal print adapted for an isometric game.
